assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reproducible room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions (1995) is an original experimental discovery with a clear observable. It opened the door to spin-dependent tunnelling devices and underpins read heads and non-volatile magnetic memory, so the benefit to society is concrete and well documented.
assessment.attribution: The 1995 room-temperature results were published near-simultaneously by Miyazaki's group and Moodera's group, and I would credit those two as the original experimenters. Parkin's later contribution (coherent MgO barriers, large TMR) is a major improvement and may count as the second wave rather than the original discovery; this should be judged against the historical record.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of independent confirmation, industrial deployment and a stable physical interpretation make recognition fully mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether Parkin's MgO-barrier work should share credit with or replace one of the 1995 discoverers.
Earlier Julliere 1975 low-temperature observation is not on the supplied credit list and sets precedent that must be weighed.
Whether the committee regards this as physics discovery or primarily device engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Flat bands at the magic angle, correlated insulator states and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened a new tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. The original experiment is clear and the field it launched is large and productive.
assessment.attribution: The prediction of the magic angle (Bistritzer and MacDonald) and the experimental observation (Jarillo-Herrero group) are clearly separable and form a natural theory-plus-experiment pairing. The supplied credit omits the first author of the experimental papers (Yuan Cao), so the experimental credit is incomplete as given; I can only propose from the listed names.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many independent groups across several moire systems since 2018, but the nature of the superconducting pairing and correlated states is still debated. Timely but the interpretation is not fully settled.
uncertainties: Interpretation of the superconductivity (pairing mechanism) remains open.
Experimental credit within the Jarillo-Herrero group beyond the listed names is not captured; I cannot verify authorship details independently.
Early theory precursors (e.g. Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) are not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, deliver fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and are an instrument that opens new measurements (relativistic geodesy, tests of constancy of constants, candidate redefinition of the second). A clear invention with tangible impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first clocks; Ye's group drove the strontium clock to record accuracy and integrated frequency-comb metrology. Two laureates is a clean configuration, though the field overlaps with the 2005 and 2012 prizes and with ion-clock work by others.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs confirm performance; the technology is stable and mature, with redefinition of the second pending.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior frequency-comb and ion-trap prizes could be read as a second-generation improvement rather than a new discovery.
Contributions of others (e.g. Ludlow, Hinkley, Vuletic-related lattice work) fall outside the supplied credits.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos in 2013 and the association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 (2017) opened a new window on the universe, and the IceCube detector is an extraordinary instrument for it.
assessment.attribution: Halzen drove the concept and the collaboration; Karle and Yoshida had major roles but IceCube is a collaboration of hundreds, so a one-to-three person attribution is difficult and the decisive individual contributions are not obvious from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed in several channels and by other detectors; source identification is still sparse beyond one or two objects, so the astrophysical picture is still developing.
uncertainties: Fair attribution within a large collaboration and with AMANDA predecessors and other early proposers.
Sparse source identification; origin of most of the flux unknown.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and quantized edge transport form a major conceptual advance in condensed matter, with the key experimental verification of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe and the quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetic topological insulator films. Experimental verification is clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) provided the theory, Molenkamp's group the 2007 HgTe observation, and Xue's group the 2013 QAH observation. Mixing QSH and QAH in one prize is plausible but gives three people spanning different effects; Bernevig, Zhang and Hasan are also in the competing record (see overlapping ballot entry). Allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by independent groups; QAH now reproduced and developed towards metrology, so timing is good.
uncertainties: Competing attribution to Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Hasan, Mele and others is handled in a different ballot entry and not resolved here.
Practical benefit to humanity is still prospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond (Gruber et al. 1997 and Jelezko et al. 2004) is an original experiment that created a room-temperature solid-state quantum sensor, used for nanoscale magnetometry and biological sensing. This is the kind of new tool that lets people see what was invisible.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup's group made the first optical detection of single NV spins and Jelezko carried out the coherent control; both are decisive. Lukin's group contributed major later work on quantum registers and sensing, but I would keep the original-experiment pair. Early Gruber/Drabenstedt authors are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced worldwide and commercially developing; stable interpretation. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether Lukin's role should be included for sensing protocols and quantum-register work.
Many of the sensing applications are still at the research stage.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Neodymium-iron-boron magnets (1982-84) are the strongest permanent magnets known and underpin electric motors, wind turbines, hard drives and consumer electronics. A clear invention with huge practical benefit, in the spirit of the prize for invention.
assessment.attribution: Sagawa (Sumitomo) and Croat (General Motors) independently announced the compound Nd2Fe14B at essentially the same time; two laureates is a natural configuration, but the independent parallel discovery and the associated patent dispute must be reviewed against the historical record.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use; thoroughly confirmed and recognition is long overdue if considered a physics prize topic.
uncertainties: Whether the committee judges it as physics rather than materials/engineering or chemistry.
Credit to other members of the Sumitomo and GM teams and to Koon and Das (precursor work) is outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics (2004) created a controllable platform for light-matter interaction on a chip and is the basis of most superconducting-qubit readout and architectures. It is an original, widely used experimental tool.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin and Schoelkopf proposed the architecture; Wallraff and Schoelkopf realised strong coupling experimentally. Four credited names exceed three; I would take the experimental originators plus the principal theorist, leaving Blais out as a difficult trade-off.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced everywhere and technologically central, but the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits may make the committee cautious about another superconducting-circuit award soon.
uncertainties: Proximity to the recent superconducting-circuit prize.
Selection of three out of four credited names is unresolved, and the contribution of others (e.g. Devoret, Nakamura) is outside this entry.
